lines.vo: Eating lunch at your screen can make you snack more later.
That's not a bigger appetite. Your brain barely noticed lunch.
Kev logs screen-free meals in his Break the Habit tracker.
In a twenty eleven study in Bristol, people ate the same lunch, some while playing a computer game.
lines.cap: In a 2011 study in Bristol, people ate the same lunch, some while playing a computer game.

lines.vo: The gamers felt less full, and remembered their lunch less clearly.
A little later, at a biscuit taste test, they ate more biscuits.
So eat away from the screen. Just you, the food, and a few slow bites.
Brain sees the meal, cravings calm down. That's how you stay on track.

hook: Eating at your *screen* makes you snack later
